aria: Animated recap of the Clippers' 139 to 123 home win over New Orleans: Kobe Sanders' go-ahead three with 2:23 left in the third quarter, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Darius Garland's 24 points and 10 assists, the top scorers, how the Clippers won, and the next game at Phoenix.
notes: Box score from the Clippers' 139–123 home win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Nov 8, 2026, from Covers.com's game overview (quarter scores, every player's line, points in the paint, fast-break points and biggest leads). All 139 Clippers points and all 123 Pelicans points are accounted for in the box score. Game details from the AP (via ABC News), Reuters/Field Level Media (via 92.1 The Ticket) and CBS Sports. The sports data feed wasn't available for this recap; records are from the site's standings after Sunday's games (Clippers 2–7, Phoenix 3–5).

Biggest leads: the Clippers' 20 (Covers.com; Field Level Media says Nick Martinelli's dunk with 1:59 left made it a game-high 20) and New Orleans' 4 (Covers.com). The Clippers' 54.8% shooting and 139 points were both season highs (AP), and their 11 turnovers a season low (Field Level Media). The win ended a seven-game losing streak and was their first since the season opener (AP). Gradey Dick's 15 was a season high (Field Level Media). The Clippers play at Phoenix on Tuesday at 9:00 PM ET (Plain Text Sports schedule; the AP says Tuesday night).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Kobe Sanders' three-pointer with 2:23 left in the third quarter that put the Clippers ahead 94–93; they never trailed again (Field Level Media). The recaps don't describe the move, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the LA Clippers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Sanders’ listed 6-foot-8 and 207 pounds (RealGM), wearing No. 4 (RealGM), with arms scaled to the 6-foot-8.3 wingspan against a measured 6-foot-7 height in his databallr draft profile. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
